## 3.10.0 — 5 Nov 2026 · The TV casino comes alive, a smoother phone app that stays connected, updates in their own window

### New

- **Teen Patti on the TV: the deal and the show**
  - Before: the cards just appeared in front of each player, and at a show the hands were simply there, face up.
  - Now: the dealer deals three cards to every seat, one at a time from the deck, starting on their left. At a show
    the hands slide out and turn over card by card, then the winning hand lifts and glows with its name in gold.
    Every screen deals and turns the same card at the same moment. Hold'em deals the same way.
- **Big Six on the TV: a real money wheel**
  - Before: a plain red pointer twitched at the top while the wheel turned.
  - Now: a leather flapper on a brass pivot leans on each brass peg and snaps back, the wheel blurs at full speed and
    sharpens as it slows, and the winning segment lights up under the flapper when it stops — in step with the panel.
- **Housie on the TV: the cage, the ball and the stamp**
  - Before: the number appeared in a big ball and its square lit up.
  - Now: a brass cage tumbles its balls as each call comes, the drawn ball rolls down a rail into the cradle, and a
    stamp marks the number on the board. Every prize claim gets its own banner — EARLY FIVE!, TOP LINE!, FULL HOUSE! —
    with the player's name and a burst of sparks.

### Better

- **Colours look right out of the box**
  - Before: a fresh install sent colours to the panel uncorrected, so mid-tones looked flat and washed out until you
    calibrated it yourself.
  - Now: every DeskDot (laptop, phone, watch and the browser app) starts with the colour settings we tuned by eye on
    a real panel: deeper mid-tones, visible shadows and richer colour. Your own calibration is never touched, and
    "DeskDot (tuned)" is the first preset (and what Reset goes back to) if you want to return to it.

- **The phone app fills the whole screen**
  - Before: the studio sat between a solid status bar at the top and a solid navigation bar at the bottom.
  - Now: it runs edge to edge under see-through bars, and nothing hides under them or under the keyboard.
- **A quick LED intro on the phone instead of "Starting DeskDot…"**
  - Before: the app opened on a "Starting DeskDot…" line, then a big sunset scene with a progress bar and tips.
  - Now: the DeskDot logo builds itself out of LED dots in about a second and a half and fades straight into the
    studio. If the engine needs a moment longer, the logo just stays lit. It follows your theme and your phone's
    animation setting.
- **A glass tab bar on the phone that you can drag**
  - Before: the bottom bar (Panel, Apps, Presets, Settings) was a flat, nearly solid strip, and you could only tap it.
  - Now: it is a floating pane of glass that blurs what scrolls under it. The bubble behind the open tab follows
    your finger along the bar, springs to the nearest tab when you let go and opens it. Tapping still works.
- **Smoother phone app**
  - Before: on a phone every change on the live panel made the whole screen redraw through an invisible grain layer,
    and the blur behind sheets redrew too, so scrolling and switching tabs could stutter.
  - Now: phones skip that layer and that blur, and the app no longer plays the studio's big intro scenes on top.

- **Updates open in their own window**
  - Before: "Update available" sent you into Settings, where the version, the notes and the Install button were mixed
    in with everything else.
  - Now: it opens an Updates window, like the panel's Connection window: your version and the new one, what's new,
    one Install button, and each step ticking off as DeskDot downloads, checks and installs the update — with a clear
    message and Retry if something goes wrong. In the browser it's one Reload.
- **The game scenes on the TV stand in your table's room**
  - Before: Snake, Pong, Tetris and the other games sat on a flat near-black page, whatever theme you picked.
  - Now: the theme's felt glow and pattern show behind the panel, and the cards wear the table's colours.
- **Nothing falls off the TV at the card tables**
  - Before: the bottom player's name plate was cut off at the bottom of the screen, and the table's name sat under
    their cards and chips.
  - Now: every seat, plate and hand fits on screen; the last move shows on the player's plate, clear of the cards.
- **A tidier Housie and Big Six board on the TV**
  - Before: the housie board ran into the table's edge and labels overlapped the balls; big six's chips covered the
    odds.
  - Now: both boards sit inside the felt, every label has its own place, and the "no winners" note fits its card.
- **No house cut at the poker and Housie tables**
  - Before: the host could set a rake, so the house kept a share of every Hold'em pot and of the Housie ticket money.
  - Now: the rake setting is gone. Every pot and every Housie prize pool goes wholly to the players who win it.

### Fixed

- **The phone no longer loops between connecting and the panel's pairing screen**
  - Before: on some phones the panel connected, then every few seconds dropped back to its pairing screen and
    reconnected, over and over — the phone's Bluetooth choked on the big packets DeskDot sent while uploading an
    animation.
  - Now: the phone sends smaller packets and waits for each one to be confirmed, so animations upload and the panel
    stays connected.
- **Back closes the sheet on the phone**
  - Before: pressing Back with Settings (or any sheet or menu) open left the app.
  - Now: Back closes what is open first; on the Apps, Presets or Settings tab it takes you to the Panel tab; only
    from the Panel tab does it go to the home screen.
- **"What's new" reads properly in Settings**
  - Before: long notes broke into stray half-lines under each item.
  - Now: every note reads as one piece, the way it was written.
- **Smoother Teen Patti and Hold'em on TV sticks**
  - Before: the card tables redrew the whole table four times a second, so they could stutter on a Fire TV.
  - Now: they only redraw when something changes; the moving cards are light sprites.
- **Everything fits on the phone screen**
  - Before: in the phone app's Settings some rows ran off the right edge (the status indicators, "What the panel
    shows"), the search box sat lower and shorter than the section buttons beside it, the Apps search was shorter than
    its view switch, and the sides of the screens had uneven margins.
  - Now: every row fits and wraps neatly on any phone, the search boxes line up with the buttons next to them, every
    screen has the same 16 px side margin, the page-theme dots fill their card evenly, and the Show / Playlist bar sits
    at the bottom even for apps with few settings.
